title: Edge SDK compact context mapper and resilient span relay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:

We need a compact context mapping layer inside the Edge SDK that converts high-entropy tracing/metadata envelopes into a tightly encoded, versioned context token for low-bandwidth transports (mobile, browser-worker, and constrained edge proxies). The token should preserve trace/span ids, sampling hints, and a small set of provenance attributes (region, origin, service-role) while intentionally excluding large baggage fields. Additionally, implement a resilient span relay that can buffer and retransmit span batches when the primary telemetry egress is unavailable, with size/age caps to avoid unbounded memory growth.

Goals:
- Reduce per-request header overhead for SDKs on constrained clients by ~60% compared to the current JSON envelope in practice tests.
- Ensure the compact token is forward-compatible: include a 1-byte version and 1-byte flags.
- Maintain traceability: ability to reconstruct the minimal context server-side for stitching with full spans emitted by other services.
- Provide a configurable local buffer (default 1MB, max 8MB) for unsent spans and graceful retries with jitter backoff.
- Offer opt-in backward compatibility mode for proxies that expect the full envelope for 30 days after rollout.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Format: CBOR-like binary with stable field IDs (not full CBOR to avoid dependency weight in tiny SDKs). We'll use a micro-encoder implemented in portable C/Go/TS to match each SDK language. The encoder will map: version:u8, flags:u8, trace_id:16 bytes (when present), span_id:8 bytes, sampled:u8, sampling_priority:i8, region:string (short id), origin:string (up to 12 chars), minimal_tags:uint8-count + packed key/value pairs (cap 3 pairs), and a 16-bit CRC for quick validation.
- Excluded baggage: arbitrary user baggage, long JSON payloads. Rationale: baggage increases header size and isn't critical for routing/fallback decisions. Teams can attach larger context via out-of-band mechanisms (console links, dashboard references).
- Security: token integrity relies on CRC only; sensitive data must not be included. If future signing is required, we will add a new version bit. For now, avoid expensive crypto in edge SDKs.
- Server reconciliation: upgrade ingestion edge to accept both compact token and legacy envelope. The ingestion layer will map compact token to internal request context and, if necessary, enrich via lookup from a short-lived cache keyed by trace_id if more provenance is required.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarked payload size: compact token <= 48 bytes median vs legacy median 120 bytes on sampled mobile traces.
- End-to-end tracing: when compaction is enabled on the client and the server is upgraded, traces must stitch and show correct parent-child relationships for 99.9% of synthetic test traces (allowing 0.1% due to carrier loss).
- Buffer behavior: under simulated egress outage (10 minutes), SDK retains <= configured buffer and retransmits in FIFO order with exponential backoff and randomized jitter. Memory usage tested across JS, Go, and Android SDKs.
- Rollout plan documented and toggleable via remote config with opt-in compatibility window.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype binary token encoder/decoder in Go (library: enc/compactctx). Add unit tests for encoding/decoding, CRC checks, and version migration.
2) Implement small port in TypeScript SDK (edge-js-sdk) and Go SDK (edge-go-sdk). Keep implementation dependency-free.
3) Add ingestion layer decoder in trace-collector service with feature flag to accept new tokens and populate request context.
4) Implement local buffer/retry in SDKs: bounded queue, soft-fail to non-blocking request path. Expose metrics: buffer_size_bytes, drops, retransmit_attempts.
5) QA: synthetic end-to-end test harness for cross-language stitching. Load test under 10k rps of compact tokens to validate collector scaling.
6) Canary rollout: enable compact headers for 5% of mobile clients, monitor spans lost, trace continuity, and p95 latency of collector decode path.

Migration and rollback:
- Start with server-side decode behind a feature flag; accept both legacy and compact tokens.
- After 2 weeks of canary with no regression, ramp to 50% and schedule 30-day compatibility window for clients on older SDKs.
- If >0.5% increase in trace gaps or >2% increase in collector CPU on decode path, rollback flag to disable compaction parsing and revert clients.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compact+Context+Mapping+Design
- Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/enc-compactctx (WIP PR: #142)
- Collection edge change: github.com/redwood-inference/trace-collector PR #389

Open questions:
- Do we need a lightweight HMAC for integrity? (Security team asked to weigh CPU cost vs tamper risk.)
- Should we include a small TTL in the token to limit replay? This increases token size by 4 bytes but helps stale context.
- Which three tag keys are most critical to allow in the compact payload? Suggestion: service_role, deployment_region, client_version. Need PM priority.
comments: 2026-02-13 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created with design summary and goals. Assigned to Diego for prototype work.
2026-02-20 Diego Alvarez: Prototyped Go encoder; median token size ~44 bytes for typical mobile sample. Pushed draft PR to enc/compactctx. Need review on field IDs and CRC choice.
2026-02-25 Security (Anika Patel): Flagged integrity concern. Requested analysis of HMAC cost on Android. Assigned follow-up security spike.

2026-03-02 Diego Alvarez: Implemented SDK buffer with default 1MB cap. Added metrics: edge.sdk.buffer_bytes, edge.sdk.dropped_spans, edge.sdk.retransmit_count. Running local e2e harness against collector in docker-compose.
2026-03-05 PM (Jordan Li): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Confirmed three tag candidates: service_role, deployment_region, client_version. Marked for inclusion in MVP.

2026-03-08 QA (Elena Russo): Synthetic stitching tests show 99.94% parent-child correctness at canary scale. Observed occasional 503 during collector decode under GC spikes — traced to allocation pattern in decoder; Diego to optimize.

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez: Optimized decoder to avoid ephemeral allocations; collector CPU drop ~18% in load tests. Preparing rollout playbook and remote-config toggle. Marking ticket ready for canary rollout.
